items.title: Video: Cristiano Ronaldo reaches 982 career goals with latest strike for Al Nassr vs Al Faisaly in Saudi Pro League
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scores a header from a Joao Felix free-kick delivery to reach 982 career goals for Al Nassr. 
Cristiano Ronaldo moved closer to one of the most remarkable milestones in football history. The Al Nassr captain scored with a header against Al Faisaly in the Saudi Pro League to reach 982 career goals, leaving him really close from the 1,000 mark.



The goal came from a free kick, which Joao Felix delivered into the box for Ronaldo to head home and extend Al Nassr’s lead to 2-0. It ended a wait for the 41-year-old, who had been stuck on 981 goals since Oct. 12, when he scored in Al Nassr’s 3-1 win over Neftchi Fargona in the AFC Champions League.



Minutes after scoring, the Portuguese forward found the net again to complete a brace, but the goal was reviewed by VAR and ultimately ruled out for offside. Ronaldo now needs 18 more goals to reach 1,000, a milestone that would be unprecedented in the modern game.



JOÃO FÉLIX WITH THE FREE KICK DELIVERY, CRISTIANO RONALDO ASCENDS ABOVE EVERYONE AND THUNDERS A HEADER HOME! 🤯🐐THE MAN IS DEFYING GRAVITY! THE AERIAL DOMINANCE, THE HANG TIME, THE SHEER IMPERIAL AUTHORITY IN THE AIR!FLYING CARS! THE GOAT IS AIRBORNE AGAIN! 🚀💛…— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 23, 2026 



Al Nassr stay firmly in the Saudi Pro League title race



With this partial victory, Al Nassr would climb to 25 points if the result holds, level with league leaders Al Qadsiah and one point ahead of third-placed Al Hilal. The leaders would remain first for now on goal difference (+15 to +14), while Al Nassr’s record would stand at eight wins, one draw and one loss.


        


The next result that could reshape the table is a direct clash at the top, as Al Hilal face Al Qadsiah in Matchday 11 today. The challengers have played nine games, one fewer than the two clubs above them, and currently sit on 24 points with the best goal difference in the league (+20).



Al Nassr would be best served by a result that stops Al Hilal from winning. A draw would keep the title race extremely tight, with Al Qadsiah just one point clear and the other two level on 25, while a victory for the leaders would at least keep the team with the game in hand from taking control at the top.



A win for the visitors would be the worst outcome, as it would put them two points clear after entering this round with a match in hand, complicating matters even further for the chasing pack.

Take a look at the projected lineups for Al-Faisaly vs Al Nassr in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al-Faisaly host Al Nassr in a Saudi Pro League fixture that pits a team scrapping for points against the two-time champions chasing continued momentum.
Al-Faisaly come into this one off a 2-2 draw with Al Shabab last Sunday, a result that followed a 3-2 win over Al Kholood on October 15. Before that stretch they were beaten 1-3 by Al Ittihad back on September 11, a reminder of the gap that still exists against the league’s top sides. A home result here would settle the nerves after that mixed run and keep Al-Faisaly clear of the bottom of the table.
Al Nassr arrive unbeaten in their last three outings, having edged Neom SC 1-0 on October 20 after a comfortable 3-0 win over Al Diriyah on October 9. They also drew 1-1 with Al Khaleej back on September 12, so the recent form has trended upward since that result. Another win would stretch their momentum further and keep the pressure on the teams above them in the standings.
Al-Faisaly confirmed lineup
Giovanni Solinas sends out a 4-3-3 built around a compact midfield of Andrei Girotto, Jaime Seoane and Abdulaziz Al Bishi, with Flavio and Mohammed Al Shanqiti supplying width from the full-back areas. Abdoulaye Seck and Yaseen Barnawi anchor the back line in front of Fernando Pacheco, while Alexandre Mendy and Abdullah Al-Mogren are tasked with stretching the Al Nassr defense alongside the central midfield trio. With no absences listed, Solinas can field his preferred XI and lean on the side’s organization to try to disrupt Al Nassr’s attacking rhythm.
Al-Faisaly confirmed starting XI (3-4-3): Fernando Pacheco, Yaseen Barnawi, Mohammed Al Shanqiti, Mohammed Jahfali, Abdoulaye Seck, Andrei Girotto, Flávio, Eid Al Muwallad, Alexandre Mendy, Abdulaziz Al Bishi, Abdullah Al Mogren. Coach: Giovanni Solinas.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Ange Postecoglou lines Al Nassr up in a 4-4-2, pairing Cristiano Ronaldo with Joao Felix up front and flanking the midfield with Sadio Mane and Angelo Gabriel for width. Inigo Martinez and Abdulelah Al Amri hold the center of defense in front of Bento Krepski, with Nawaf Al-Boushail and Ayman Yahya pushing on from full-back to support the attack. There are no absences to work around, which means Postecoglou can field a settled, attack-minded unit built to carry the recent winning form into the away fixture.

A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou, the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. items.title: Thibaut Courtois uses Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi to defend Vinicius Junior amid form struggles
items.description:
Thibaut Courtois defended Vinicius Junior by comparing the criticism he faces to that of Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi. 
Thibaut Courtois has come to the defense of Vinicius Junior, and he did it by naming two of the greatest players in history. After Real Madrid’s 4-1 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League, the Belgian goalkeeper said that Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi are the only players he knows who perform at their best every season, and that even they faced criticism.



Courtois spoke to the media in the mixed zone at the Santiago Bernabeu, where he was asked about Vinicius’ dip in form. “I think he’s searching for his best form, and I’m confident he’ll find it with the support of the team and the fans,” he said. “In my opinion, he played a good match. I saw him create chances and pose a threat, but sometimes things don’t go as planned”.



The goalkeeper then used Ronaldo and Messi as an example. “As for players who consistently perform at their best season after season, I only know two: Cristiano and Messi,” Courtois said. “I’ve seen them at their peak year after year, yet even these two, among the greatest in history, have faced criticism at certain points”.



Courtois also stressed that Vinicius has carried a heavy workload, saying the Brazilian has been playing almost every match for nine years. “That’s why we have to help him find that best version,” he said, adding that Vinicius is the first person who wants to be happy and perform at his best.



Vinicius Jr. of Real Madrid. (Getty Images)



A difficult season start for Vinicius



Vinicius has only one goal this season, and it came in the 4-1 win over Real Sociedad in LaLiga, a match in which he also added an assist. Since then, he has gone nine games without scoring: six in LaLiga and three in the Champions League.


        


The Brazilian has contributed three assists in LaLiga, against Real Sociedad, Malaga and Rayo, but he has not recorded a goal or an assist in any of his three Champions League appearances.



His season took another turn when he was sent off against Villarreal for pulling an opponent’s hair, just 20 minutes after coming on as a substitute. The moment of indiscipline led to a four-match ban that has already cost him the game against Sevilla.



The suspension will also keep him out of El Clasico against Barcelona on Oct. 25, as well as the matches against Racing Santander and Valencia. It has made Vinicius a target of criticism, and his return to LaLiga will not come until the match against Celta on Nov. 21.

items.title: Why is Christian Pulisic not starting for Milan vs Bournemouth in 2026-27 UEFA Europa League?
items.description:
The American forward’s absence from the starting XI comes at a crucial point in Milan’s campaign, as the Italian club looks to build on consecutive victories and improve its position in Europe. 
Christian Pulisic will not start for Milan against Bournemouth in the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League, with head coach Ruben Amorim having made significant changes to his lineup. The American forward’s absence from the starting XI comes at a crucial point in Milan’s campaign, as the Italian club looks to build on consecutive victories and improve its position in Europe.



Milan travels to the south coast of England after a convincing 4-0 victory over Red Bull Salzburg and a hard-fought 3-2 win against Atalanta in Serie A. However, with several players unavailable and another demanding stretch of fixtures approaching, Amorim has opted for a different attacking combination against a Bournemouth side that has won both of its opening Europa League matches.



Bournemouth enters the contest with six points from its first two Europa League fixtures, having beaten Real Sociedad 2-1 away before defeating Sturm Graz 3-0 at home. The English club has made an impressive start to its first European campaign and will see Milan’s visit as an opportunity to strengthen its position in the competition.



The Rossoneri, meanwhile, recovered from a 2-0 opening defeat against Benfica with their emphatic victory in Salzburg. Another positive result would help Amorim’s side maintain its progress, although the visitors must contend with an opponent that has shown considerable attacking confidence.



Your Rossoneri team for tonight’s game 👊 https://t.co/ic57kcCQFE— AC Milan (@acmilan) October 22, 2026




The reason why Pulisic is not starting against Bournemouth



Pulisic has been left out of Milan’s starting lineup as Amorim rotates his squad and gives other attacking players an opportunity. According to the official lineups, the coach has switched to a 4-2-3-1 formation, prioritizing Alphadjo Cisse in a central attacking role, with Omari Hutchinson, Diego Moreira, and Ruben Loftus-Cheek providing support up front.



The decision comes as Milan manages a busy schedule, with several matches approaching in October, including the Derby della Madonnina against Inter. Amorim has already demonstrated his willingness to make wholesale changes, rotating seven players before the Salzburg victory and making another seven alterations for the subsequent Serie A match against Atalanta.



Pulisic is therefore among the players expected to begin on the bench rather than lead the team’s attack from the opening whistle. His absence from the starting XI is understood to be a selection and rotation decision, rather than confirmation of a fresh injury.



Christian Pulisic of AC Milan looks on



Alphadjo Cisse gets the starting opportunity



The biggest attacking decision concerns Cisse, who will lead the line despite Francesco Camarda being another option following Goncalo Ramos’ injury. The young Italian impressed against Salzburg, scoring a hat-trick in Milan’s 4-0 victory and strengthening his case for another prominent role.



According to previous reports from Gazzetta dello Sport, Amorim had already decided to trust Cisse as the central striker against Bournemouth. The forward’s finishing and ability to operate inside the penalty area appear to have convinced the coach that he can offer a different dimension to Milan’s attack.



With Pulisic expected to start among the substitutes, Milan will look to Hutchinson, Moreira and Cisse to provide the attacking energy needed against Bournemouth. The coach will hope that the changes preserve freshness without disrupting the momentum his team has developed over the past week.

Take a look at the projected lineups for Al Nassr vs Neom SC in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al Nassr host Neom SC in a Saudi Pro League fixture that pits a side chasing consistency against one still searching for rhythm in the final third.
Al Nassr enter on the back of a 3-0 win over Al Diriyah on October 9, a result that followed a 1-1 draw with Al Khaleej on September 12 and a 2-1 win over Abha on September 9. They have taken four points from their last two matches after that opening win, and three points here would keep them firmly in the title conversation. Postecoglou’s side will want to build on the attacking output from the Al Diriyah game rather than repeat the stalemate against Al Khaleej.
Neom SC arrive having lost 0-1 to Al-Ettifaq last Saturday, a result sandwiched between a 1-1 draw with Al Hazem on October 10 and a 4-2 win over Al Fateh FC back on September 13. The Al-Ettifaq defeat snapped whatever momentum they built from that high-scoring win in September, and they have managed just one point from their last two outings. A positive result at Al Nassr would steady a form line that has gone from free-scoring to stretched thin in recent weeks.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Postecoglou lines Al Nassr up in a 4-4-2 with Bento Krepski in goal behind a back four of Nawaf Al-Boushail, Mohamed Simakan, Iñigo Martínez and Awad Aman. Kingsley Coman and Samu provide the width in midfield, with Abdullah Al-Khaibari also in the engine room, while Sadio Mané, João Félix and Cristiano Ronaldo are all named in attacking positions. That gives the hosts three recognized forwards to rotate around a front two, suggesting fluid interchange rather than a fixed strike partnership. With no absences listed, this looks close to a full-strength selection for Al Nassr.

Neom SC confirmed lineup
Christophe Galtier also sets Neom SC up in a 4-4-2, with Marcin Bulka in goal and a back line of Khalifah Al-Dawsari, Malang Sarr, Nathan Zézé and Hawsawi Ahmed. Giorgos Masouras and Abdulmalik Al-Oyayari flank a central midfield pairing of Valentín Vada and Mohannad Abu Taha, feeding a front two of Alexandre Lacazette and Saïd Benrahma. items.title: Michael Carrick apologizes to Manchester United fans after humiliating 4-1 Como demolition
items.description:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick offered a direct apology to traveling supporters and shouldered collective blame after an abject 4-1 Champions League defeat to Italian newcomers Como. 
Manchester United traveled to Italy to face Como 1907 in the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League, only to return to England on the end of a resounding 4–1 defeat that intensifies the scrutiny surrounding head coach Michael Carrick following a difficult run of results.



Matchday 3 proved to be a chastening evening for Manchester United, as the Premier League side was thoroughly outplayed by Cesc Fabregas’ side at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. The setback compounded a troubled start to the campaign and placed Carrick under heightened pressure, with the manager walking directly to the travelling supporters at the final whistle to offer an apology for the team’s performance.



“I can only apologise to our fans. No excuses,” Michael Carrick said after the game. “I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters, they’re the heartbeat and always will be.”



Manchester United need a change of direction



The current campaign has proved exceptionally demanding for Manchester United across all fronts. With only one win from three Champions League fixtures, their domestic fortunes are equally concerning: they sit 13th in the Premier League standings, having collected just seven points from a possible 21 to remain uncomfortably close to the relegation places.



Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)



This heavy loss against Como could prove pivotal not only for Carrick’s immediate job security, but also for the wider club hierarchy and playing squad, both of whom face intense criticism over a string of underwhelming tactical setups and substandard individual displays.


        


Having fought to return to the Champions League this season, failing to qualify for next year’s edition would represent a significant sporting and financial blow. Consistency remains the fundamental challenge for the Red Devils, whose erratic form on the pitch continues to undermine their ability to establish momentum and compete effectively at the highest level of European soccer.

items.title: Why was Bukayo Saka subbed off by Arsenal vs Bayern Munich in the 2026-27 Champions League?
items.description:
Bukayo Saka was substituted off early against Bayern Munich after appearing to hurt his left knee while making a pass. 
Bukayo Saka was substituted off by Arsenal early in the Champions League match against Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena, and the reason appears to be an injury to his left knee.



The England winger went down in the opening minutes after appearing to hurt himself while making a pass. Replays showed that he did not make full contact with the ball, and Saka needed medical attention on the pitch before it became clear he could not continue.



Saka was replaced by Eberechi Eze, who took his place in the attacking line alongside Martin Odegaard and Noni Madueke, behind Kai Havertz. The change forced Mikel Arteta to rethink his plan early in a demanding away match against one of Europe’s strongest teams.



The setback is a major concern for Arteta at a crucial moment. Arsenal arrive in Munich with a perfect record in the competition, after a 1-0 win over Napoli and a 3-0 win over Lille, and they are the only team yet to concede in this season’s league phase. Saka has been one of the team’s key attackers, and the extent of the injury will be closely watched in the coming days.



pic.twitter.com/TohtAZMfIQ— TopCee (@TopceeX) October 21, 2026 



First injury concern of the season for Saka



The scare against Bayern is Saka’s first injury setback of the 2026-27 campaign. Last season, the winger missed 11 matches across all competitions, according to Transfermarkt, because of three separate problems: a hamstring injury in August and September, a hip issue in January and February, and an Achilles problem in April.


        


The Achilles injury was the most serious, as it kept him out of five matches in a decisive stretch. Saka missed Arsenal’s FA Cup quarterfinal, both legs of their Champions League quarterfinal against Sporting, and Premier League matches against Bournemouth and Manchester City. He returned in time to play in the Champions League semifinals and in the final against PSG on May 30, a defeat on penalties.



Arsenal are expected to provide an update on Saka’s condition in the coming hours. Until then, Mikel Arteta may have to plan for the coming weeks without one of his key attackers.

items.title: Why is Luis Diaz not starting for Bayern Munich vs Arsenal in 2026-27 UEFA Champions League?

The Colombian winger starts on the bench despite scoring a hat trick in the […] 
Luis Diaz is not in the starting lineup for Bayern Munich as the Bundesliga champions host Arsenal in one of the biggest games of the Champions League league phase, and the reason appears to be a tactical decision by Vincent Kompany.



The Colombian winger starts on the bench despite scoring a hat trick in the 6-1 win over RB Leipzig on Oct. 17. Bayern have not reported any injury or suspension for Diaz, and Kompany has not explained the decision, so it looks like a choice made for tactical reasons.



In his place, Kompany decided to start Alphonso Davies on the left wing, behind Harry Kane. The attack will look very different from the one that took the field in the 3-3 draw against Viking on the previous matchday, as Michael Olise is suspended and unavailable for this match.



Kompany’s decision to leave Diaz on the bench can be read as a more defensive approach. With Davies in his place on the left, Bayern gain a player who can help in defense against the attacks of Bukayo Saka and Jurrien Timber.




Our starting XI for tonight! 🌟 pic.twitter.com/w87KMd9LqP— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) October 21, 2026




Lineups confirmed



Without Joshua Kimmich and Olise, Vincent Kompany has gone with Bischof and Pavlovic in midfield. Manuel Neuer starts in goal despite being a doubt with a foot issue, while Davies, Gnabry and Saibari support Harry Kane in attack.


        


Bayern confirmed lineup: Neuer (C); Laimer, Upamecano, Min-jae Kim, Stanisic; Bischof, Pavlovic; Gnabry, Saibari, Davies; Kane.



Arteta has gone with Kai Havertz as his lone striker, leaving Viktor Gyokeres on the bench alongside Mikel Merino. Noni Madueke starts on the right wing alongside Bukayo Saka, with Eberechi Eze among the substitutes, while Jurrien Timber returns at right back.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo warned national team comeback could trigger fresh problems as ex-Portugal boss sets out return conditions
items.description:
As debate continues over his fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus, a former Portugal manager has warned that the next step could prove crucial to preventing another damaging confrontation. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future with Portugal remains uncertain despite the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF)’s decision to impose a backdated suspension that could allow him to return for November’s Nations League fixtures. As debate continues over his fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus, a former Portugal manager has warned that the next step could prove crucial to preventing another damaging confrontation.



The 41-year-old Al-Nassr forward received a 30-day ban and a €255 ($286) fine after leaving Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen in September. Although the punishment has largely run its course, Coelho believes the federation must handle the captain’s potential return carefully if it wants to avoid reopening the dispute.



Speaking to Radio Renascença’s Bola Branca, Humberto Coelho backed the decision to suspend Ronaldo but criticized the financial penalty as ineffective. “Ronaldo’s suspension was important, but the fine is a bit out of place and doesn’t help at all,” the former Selecao manager said.



Coelho also argued that the incident should never have escalated to the point where disciplinary action became necessary. “What I know for sure is that if I were the coach, this wouldn’t have happened. That’s for sure. And if I were a player, I don’t think it would have happened either,” he explained.









As a former national team captain himself, Coelho believes the episode reflects a breakdown in responsibility on multiple sides. He described the situation as complicated and expressed concern about the damage it could cause to both Ronaldo and the FPF.



How Ronaldo’s dispute with Jorge Jesus escalated



The controversy began during the national team’s September international window, when Ronaldo was an unused substitute in the national team’s 2-1 victory over Norway. The forward later claimed that Jesus had given him assurances about his involvement before deciding against using him.



Ronaldo subsequently left Portugal’s camp on September 30, ahead of the Nations League match against Denmark. In a public statement, he accused Jesus of an “absolute breach of trust,” while the coach denied that the two had made the agreement Ronaldo described.



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal reacts



The FPF disciplinary council eventually found Ronaldo guilty of an offence under Article 160(1) of its disciplinary regulations. On October 19, the federation announced a 30-day suspension and a symbolic monetary fine, taking into account mitigating circumstances that included Ronaldo’s contributions to football and his recent disciplinary record.



The conditions Ronaldo must meet before returning



Coelho made clear that he would welcome Ronaldo back to Portugal, but stressed that the return must be properly prepared. He believes responsibility cannot rest solely on the player, with the national team coach and federation president also needing to help rebuild trust. “I’d like him to return. The right conditions have to be in place, and that’s up to the coach, the president and Cristiano,” Coelho said.



Pedro Proenca, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Jorge Jesus



He added that the three parties must establish genuine understanding and accept responsibility for their respective roles in resolving the dispute. A return without proper preparation and shared accountability could create further problems rather than settle the existing tensions.



Coelho delivered his strongest warning when discussing what might happen if the situation is mishandled. “If his return isn’t properly planned and prepared, with a strong sense of responsibility from everyone involved, there’s no point in it. Otherwise, serious problems could resurface.”

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal fine mocked as Spanish Journalist spots one hilarious double-standards detail
items.description:
The punishment has attracted attention far beyond Portugal, with a Spanish journalist delivering a sarcastic assessment that has sparked amusement and raised questions about the severity of the decision. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has found himself at the center of another international soccer controversy after the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced disciplinary action against the legendary forward. However, the punishment has attracted attention far beyond Portugal, with a Spanish journalist delivering a sarcastic assessment that has sparked amusement and raised questions about the severity of the decision.



The Al-Nassr captain received a suspension following his departure from Portugal’s national team camp ahead of a Nations League fixture against Denmark in September. While the ruling could have consequences for his relationship with national team coach Jorge Jesus, it was one particular aspect of the punishment that prompted Juanma Castano’s most memorable response.



The FPF’s Disciplinary Council handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension and a €255 ($286) fine after he left the national team camp before Portugal’s Nations League match against Denmark in Copenhagen on September 30. According to the disciplinary ruling, Ronaldo informed federation president Pedro Proenca that he was “not in the right frame of mind to remain with the squad.”



The forward reportedly left Parken Stadium in a vehicle requested through the federation’s director of services as Portugal prepared for a training session. The decision followed a disagreement between Ronaldo and Jesus over the forward’s involvement in the Selecao’s matches. Ronaldo subsequently accused the coach of breaking promises about his playing time and failing to deliver a public clarification they had reportedly agreed upon.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



In a statement released on October 6, Ronaldo criticized what he described as Jesus’s “authoritarian, ‘I’m in charge here’ attitude.” The dispute has raised questions about whether the two will be able to move forward together, although the suspension’s timing could allow Ronaldo to return for Portugal’s November fixtures.



Hilarious comparison emerges



Speaking on Spanish radio programme El Partidazo de COPE, Juanma Castano reacted sarcastically to the FPF’s decision, suggesting that the federation had been particularly severe with Ronaldo in one respect while barely affecting him financially.



“The Portuguese Federation isn’t messing around. They’ve slapped him with a 30-day suspension—even though he hasn’t been called up—but the suspension counts from the previous training camp, from the very day he left,” Castano said.



        View this post on Instagram            




He explained that the suspension had effectively been running since the incident, meaning Ronaldo could become eligible for Portugal’s next squad selection once the sanction expires. The journalist then turned his attention to the financial penalty, setting up the punchline that made his comments stand out.



“But they did hit him where it hurts—in his wallet. That’s where they decided to get serious: the ‘cash.’ Cristiano has been fined 255 euros,” Castano joked. He followed with the comparison that quickly became the defining moment of his reaction: “Damn, in any Spanish city, you’d get a 300-euro fine just for taking the trash out at the wrong time—that’s more expensive than deserting the Portuguese national team!”



What helped reduce the punishment



The disciplinary ruling also revealed that Ronaldo’s representatives requested mitigating circumstances based on his contributions to soccer, his sporting achievements and his assistance in establishing the facts of the case. The FPF accepted the arguments relating to his significant service to soccer and his sporting merits, but rejected the claim that he had made a decisive contribution to uncovering the truth.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal holds the UEFA Nations League trophy 



The committee explained that this particular mitigating factor applied to disciplinary cases that were difficult to investigate. The decision has also attracted ridicule beyond Spain, with an English BBC panel reportedly questioning the modest size of the fine and joking about Ronaldo submitting his sporting résumé as part of his defence.

items.title: Julian Alvarez joins Lionel Messi among Argentina’s all-time top Champions League scorers
items.description:
Julian Alvarez ended a 174-day goal drought and joined Lionel Messi among Argentina’s top Champions League scorers. 
Julian Alvarez has joined Lionel Messi among the most prolific Argentine scorers in Champions League history. The Atletico Madrid striker scored in the 1-1 draw at Stuttgart, ending a long scoring drought and lifting his career total in the competition to 26 goals.



Atletico Madrid went into the break trailing after Leweling put Stuttgart ahead in the 36th minute. Alvarez answered early in the second half, finishing a cross from Lookman first time into the top corner in the 47th minute, scoring his first goal of the season for Atletico.



The goal also ended the longest drought of Alvarez’s career. He had not scored since Apr. 29, when he found the net in the 1-1 draw against Arsenal in last season’s Champions League semifinal, a gap of 174 days.



Coach Diego Simeone was full of praise for his forward after the match, especially for the effort he put in on the night. “The game he played was with incredible physical effort,” Simeone said. “He worked parts of the match as an inside forward on the left. The goal was a golazo and it makes me very happy for him, we need him.”




⚽️🕷️ pic.twitter.com/I45FXUEbqV— Atlético de Madrid (@Atleti) October 20, 2026




The Atletico Madrid manager also stressed how important the World Cup winner is to his team. Simeone described Alvarez as “decisive in getting to the places we need to reach” and made a request: “Let’s hope that little by little he starts to find himself again with what he showed us today”.


        


Alvarez moves into elite company



With the goal, Alvarez moved past Hernan Crespo, who sits on 25, and now ranks among the top five Argentine scorers in Champions League history. Only Messi, Alfredo Di Stefano, Sergio Aguero and Lautaro Martinez have scored more.



PlayerGoals1. Lionel Messi1292. Alfredo Di Stefano493. Sergio Aguero414. Lautaro Martinez275. Julian Alvarez266. Hernan Crespo25



Alvarez will now try to build on his goal as Atletico Madrid look to turn their Champions League campaign around. With four points from three matches, the team will need its forward at his best, and the numbers suggest he is on his way to climbing even higher on Argentina’s all-time list.

Cristiano Ronaldo sends emotional message to Kvaratskhelia after PSG winger’s ACL injury
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo sent an emotional message to Kvaratskhelia after the PSG winger tore his ACL against Barcelona. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has reached out to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia after the PSG winger suffered a season-ending injury. The Al Nassr star sent a message of support to Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in PSG’s 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona.



The Portuguese star left a heartfelt message of encouragement for the Georgian in a comment on the post in which the PSG player announced his diagnosis after the injury against Barcelona.



“The hardest battles in football are often ones nobody sees,” Cristiano wrote. “I know that feeling, Kvara. But never forget what brought you this far, and don’t let a difficult moment make you doubt how far you can go. Keep that fire on. Your best is still to come”.



The words carry extra weight because of who they come from. Kvaratskhelia has made it clear on several occasions that Ronaldo is his childhood idol. The two shared a moment at Euro 2024, when Georgia beat Portugal 2-0 and Kvaratskhelia swapped shirts with his hero. Now, at the lowest point of his career, that same idol has told him that his best is still to come.



Cristiano Ronaldo shakes hands with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia during the Euro 2024. (Getty Images)



When could Kvaratskhelia return?



PSG have not put a timeline on Kvaratskhelia’s recovery, and the club only confirmed that he will undergo surgery in the coming days. A rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament typically keeps players out for around nine months, and projections suggest that a return could come around July 2027. That would likely rule him out for the rest of the 2026-27 season, including the decisive stretch of the Champions League and Ligue 1.


        


The injury is a major setback for a player who had played 11 times for PSG this season and was making his first start of the campaign in the Champions League when he went down.



Apart from the Georgian, PSG also suffered injuries to Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos in the match against Barcelona. The forward sustained a left thigh injury while the defender picked up a right thigh injury, and both join Nuno Mendes on the French side’s injury list.



With Kvaratskhelia out for a long spell and three more key players sidelined, PSG will have to lean on their depth as they try to defend their Champions League crown.

items.title: PSG suffer triple injury blow after Champions League win over Barcelona as Kvaratskhelia tears ACL
items.description:
PSG beat Barcelona 4-2, but Kvaratskhelia tore his ACL while Dembele and Marquinhos also went down injured. 
PSG picked up a huge result, but it may have come at a heavy price. The reigning Champions League winners beat Barcelona 4-2 at the Parc des Princes to stay perfect in the competition, yet three of their key players left the pitch with injuries. The most serious blow is Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s, who will miss a long stretch of the season.



The club confirmed that Kvaratskhelia suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. He went down early in the second half after a challenge with Barcelona’s Xavi Espart and could not put any weight on his leg as he was helped off.



PSG confirmed he will undergo surgery in the coming days and did not give a timetable for his return. The 25-year-old was making his first start of the season in the Champions League and has played 11 times for the club this campaign.



Kvaratskhelia reacted to the news on social media. “Why me? I was not ready for this,” he wrote, before promising to come back stronger for the fans who support him.




❤️‍🩹 Khvicha Kvaratskhelia: “Why me? I was not ready for this”.“Many people have asked me questions about this setback, many have said that if all the footballers in the world prayed, the match would end in a draw. That might be true, but before every match I play, I ask God to… pic.twitter.com/nmWiZVdbbg— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) October 21, 2026




Despite losing one of their stars for the rest of the season, the night still ended in celebration for PSG. The game was level at 2-2 heading into the final 10 minutes, and the hosts scored twice late to keep their Champions League defense on track with three wins from three.


        


Dembele, Marquinhos and Mendes join the injury list



Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos were also forced off against Barcelona. PSG announced that Dembele has a left thigh injury and Marquinhos a right thigh injury, and both “will remain under treatment for the next few weeks”.



While the club did not specify exact return dates for either player, neither is expected to be available for the next Ligue 1 match on Oct. 25, when PSG face Lyon.



The list of absentees was already growing before the match. Nuno Mendes suffered a left thigh injury against Strasbourg on Oct. 17 and was ruled out for the next few weeks, which means he will not be available for the trip to Lyon either. 



With Mendes, Dembele and Marquinhos all sidelined alongside Kvaratskhelia, PSG will have to rotate heavily across defense and attack in the coming fixtures.

items.title: Raphinha brushes aside 4-2 PSG defeat as Barcelona shift focus to El Clasico vs Real Madrid
items.description:
Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the 2026–27 campaign on Tuesday night, falling 4–2 to defending European champions Paris Saint-Germain in a pulsating UEFA Champions League encounter at the Parc des Princes. 
Barcelona’s unbeaten run came to an end at the worst possible time, falling to Paris Saint-Germain just days before they face Real Madrid in La Liga for El Clásico—a match that could dramatically reshape the season for both sides.



Raphinha returned to Barcelona’s starting lineup following an injury that had sidelined him in recent weeks. While the winger acknowledged that the defeat against PSG arrived at a terrible time, he emphasized that the squad cannot afford to lose focus ahead of Sunday’s crucial showdown against Real Madrid.



“We’ve only lost three points. Now we need to be ready for El Clásico. Focus,” Raphinha said after the game. Hansi Flick supported his statements by sharing that they are now preparing for the duel against Real Madrid.



A reality check



Remaining unbeaten throughout an entire season is practically impossible, especially given the grueling schedule and fierce competition top clubs face across multiple tournaments. Barcelona’s winning streak concluded after 11 consecutive victories, but this reality check may ultimately be exactly what the squad needed.



Raphinha of FC Barcelona waves to the fans as he warms up



Suffering a defeat before El Clásico could prove beneficial for Barcelona. By absorbing a difficult loss against elite opposition, they can now clearly identify the tactical flaws that require immediate attention, helping them prevent another setback against their arch-rivals in a fixture that always carries massive ramifications for both clubs’ campaigns.


        


While PSG are widely regarded as one of the most formidable teams in world football today—presenting a very different challenge than Real Madrid’s current setup—El Clásico operates under its own laws. It remains a fiercely contested, high-intensity encounter where recent form often matters little, as both clubs routinely elevate their performances to avoid defeat in such a pivotal clash.



Barcelona made key mistakes against PSG



PSG boast one of the most dangerous attacks in Europe, meaning no team can afford complacency against them. Unfortunately for Barcelona, careless turnovers and loose distribution proved costly, leaving their back line repeatedly exposed to the French side’s clinical forwards.



This defeat must be taken very seriously by Hansi Flick. With Real Madrid’s attack gaining significant momentum in recent weeks and the defense standing out as Barcelona’s most vulnerable area amid recent injuries, tightening the back line is essential ahead of Sunday.

items.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
items.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real BetisWhen at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said.At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that, whatever that was, in Istanbul – an “almost rabona”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote. Continue reading...

items.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast teamSign up for our free newsletter hereFor two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes.This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

items.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
items.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community  still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career“The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.”McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

items.title: A perfect stunt: Two Russian daredevils climb world’s second tallest building
items.description:
A video filmed using head mounted cameras of two gutsy Russians scaling China's Shanghai Tower without ropes or any climbing gear has gone viral.
Vadim Makhorov and Vitaliy Raskalov not only climbed to the top of the Shanghai Tower, but also scaled a crane on top of the building. The pair sneaked into the building site at midnight on Chinese New Year and spent almost two hours climbing up 120 floors to reach a height of 650 metres.
